Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Hi John / Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through your use case today. Quick recap and a recommended shortlist to kick off the evals we discussed.

Recap (2 mins):
- Demo covered ingest pipeline, typical prompt patterns, latency SLO of ~200–300ms p50 for single-request completions, and safety/ hallucination concerns for factual extraction.
- You'll want strong accuracy on entity extraction + concise summaries at scale.

Recommended shortlist (priority order):
1) redwood-rlhf-13B-v1 (recommended pilot) — Best quality for your extraction prompts; higher cost but lowest hallucination on our benchmarks (~2.3% factual errors on our internal QA set). Latency: ~260ms p50 on c6g-like GPU.
2) redwood-quant-7B-q4 — Good quality/cost balance; lower token cost, slightly higher hallucination (~3.8%), latency ~180ms p50. Great for higher throughput.
3) open-llama-7b-q4f16 (community) — Lowest cost, fastest latency (~140ms p50) but needs prompt engineering to hit accuracy targets; higher variance on longer context.

Attachments/links:
- acme_model_shortlist.xlsx (attached) — side-by-side cost/latency/quality comparison and recommended pilot config.
- Benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-Benchmarks (includes prompt sets and eval artifacts).

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm which two models you'd like to pilot (we recommend starting with redwood-rlhf-13B-v1 + redwood-quant-7B-q4).
- Can you share a small sample (up to 1k records) of your production prompts/expected inputs for a quick in-house eval? We can run it within the week of Mar 9.
- Let me know budget guardrails so I can include a tailored cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted.

I'll loop in Rishi and Stephanie to scope the pilot and provide a preliminary cost estimate.

Thanks,

John —

Great questions, answered inline below and added a couple items for transparency.

1) Hallucination / factuality (high level):
- redwood-rlhf-13B-v1: ~2.3% factual error rate on our internal extraction-focused eval set (this is the dataset we use for entity-level precision/recall; our tests include adversarial paraphrases similar to your examples).
- redwood-quant-7B-q4: ~3.8% factual error rate, tends to be slightly less robust on long multi-entity inputs.
- open-llama-7b-q4f16: ~6.1% factual error rate on the same eval set — requires prompt tuning to approach the 13B baseline.

Notes: those numbers are for the baseline prompt-set in the shared Drive. If you share a small sample of your actual prompts/responses we'll run the exact eval and return per-prompt failure modes.

2) Pilot hosting and timeline:
- Hosted: fastest to start (within 24–48 hours), but data will be processed via our hosted control plane (we can discuss PDP and DPA terms).
- Dedicated: fully isolated GPU pool, supports customer-managed VPC peering and tighter network controls; typical onboarding 2–3 weeks (shorter if approved by infra team).
- Private (on-prem): available for enterprise customers; timing depends on infra readiness — usually 6–8 weeks.

3) Ballpark cost (200k tokens/day):
- redwood-rlhf-13B-v1 (Hosted): ~ $1,250/day (includes generation + eval overhead).
- redwood-quant-7B-q4 (Hosted): ~ $420/day.
- Dedicated unit-estimate: ~30–40% lower per-token at commit tiers vs Hosted; I've attached a short estimate (acme_cost_estimate.pdf) with a committed-capacity example.

Attachments/links:
- acme_cost_estimate.pdf (attached) — quick Hosted vs Dedicated scenarios.
- Full benchmark results (per-prompt): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-Benchmarks

Pilot proposal (recommended):
- Duration: 2 weeks of eval runs on your sample set + 1 week of integration testing.
- Models: redwood-rlhf-13B-v1 + redwood-quant-7B-q4.
- Goal: hit <=3% factual error on extraction prompts and meet p50 latency <=300ms.

If that works I'll schedule a quick kickoff with Rishi (pricing/ops) and Stephanie (CS) to finalize the scope.

Best,
Marissa
